verdict.rationale: Consensus ships the Consensus Meter. For a yes/no question it classifies each relevant paper as supporting, refuting, or mixed/inconclusive, then displays the distribution. This directly shows where sources agree and disagree rather than giving one unqualified answer, and every response carries citations back to the sources. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of the Meter's accuracy, and evidence of agreement/disagreement views for non-yes/no questions.

support.subject: As an analyst, I can see where sources agree and disagree instead of a single unqualified answer

citations.quote: classifies each relevant paper as supporting, refuting, or mixed/inconclusive, then displays the distribution
aggregates per-study verdicts (Yes / No / Possibly / Mixed / Unknown) into a single distribution for a yes/no research question
Every response includes citations, so you can trace each insight back to the original source.
